searchText: I've been thinking more about how an issue like an invalid withdrawal root applies to ePBS: https://github.com/flashbots/mev-boost/issues/661. I don't think it applies much because in ePBS, the proposer gets unconditional payment with an invalid execution block. However, in mev-boost, the proposer defaults to local block building. Does that imply we have an asymmetry where we should add `withdrawals_root` to `ExecutionPayloadHeader` and allow the proposer to filter it out? <@755590043632140352> I don't think so, in fact I'm thinking in moving all of processing withdrawals to the payload directly, it's cleaner I think I hit an actual forkchoice bug, after a missed epoch I am not advancing the chain 😦 Ok, let me clarify my question. Today in MEV-Boost, a proposer can manually check if the withdrawals root matches what it has in the beacon state and filter builder bids based on that. In epbs, a proposer can't do it; it could sign a bid with an invalid withdrawals root but still get paid regardless. That's a mental shift. Sure, we can move processing withdrawals to the payload, that makes this argument moot... I think this is kinda irrelevant, the builder can always invalidate it's own payload. It could prevent a very specific bug in the builder that has the right beacon block root as parent and has the wrong state transition, I do not see what's the gain here I think you get slightly better liveness. The difference is that the proposer has a choice to prevent a missing execution slot. If you take the withdrawal issue above and apply it to epbs today, the execution slot is missed, but in MEV-Boost, it defaults to local building Notice that today the problem when the builder has the wrong withdrawals is because it's building over the wrong block. On ePBS you already commit to a parent block root I buy this argument. Instead of checking withdrawals root, checking the parent block hash/root is good enough to prevent this Oh I think I have a pretty bad bug on forkchoice 😦 What is it? 🙂 weight counting is wrong just happy case? or reveal status + new boost values are in play? how could it have the wrong block? `getHeader` specifies the parent hash that's simply a bug that's the same guarantee you describe above yeah but that bug is that they are building over the wrong beaconstate, but yeah hash is just as good as root here right, but if they manage to get the wrong beaconstate (therefore withdrawals) already, it won't be better or worse this way I think it's still kinda irrelevant, if a builder is giving bad blocks on ePBS, proposers can immediately block it because that wrong beacon is already a bug, not a hole in the API yeah definitely I think builders bugs are kinda irrelevant how can the proposer know that from just the bid itself? because today you can withdrawals_root is part of the header yeah that is a regression or potentially in any case it's a bug that would cause bad incentives if fixed like that: rational proposers would still prefer to include the bad bid of course we can make it part of state transition > rational proposers would still prefer to include the bad bid That wont be the client code though. We check withdralwas root and use local block if it fails which transition it's part of is partly a question of who should bear the risk anyway, this is extra complexity without any reason, it's much simpler to just move withdrawals to the payload ya, I tend to agree with this Anyway, I'll continue debugging forkchoice which is a bit of a mess sure, it's at least not worse than today then in epbs, we can do better circuit breaker too, we can block the builder if we immediate see one invalid execution payload from them Whomever decided to have an executable spec is a genius, it's trully the best protocol bug bounty program I've ever seen, it pays for itself ``` ========================= 3 failed, 756 passed, 432 skipped, 34 warnings in 492.69s (0:08:12) ========================= ``` Almost there, getting the withholding forkchoice tests failing these are pretty nasty to figure out what the hell is wrong of if there is something wrong, it could easily be (block, slot) voting at play. Hoping to have this ready tomorrow

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
I've been thinking more about how an issue like an invalid withdrawal root applies to ePBS: https://github.com/flashbots/mev-boost/issues/661.

I don't think it applies much because in ePBS, the proposer gets unconditional payment with an invalid execution block. However, in mev-boost, the proposer defaults to local block building.

Does that imply we have an asymmetry where we should add `withdrawals_root` to `ExecutionPayloadHeader` and allow the proposer to filter it out? <@755590043632140352>

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I don't think so, in fact I'm thinking in moving all of processing withdrawals to the payload directly, it's cleaner

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I think I hit an actual forkchoice bug, after a missed epoch I am not advancing the chain 😦

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Ok, let me clarify my question. Today in MEV-Boost, a proposer can manually check if the withdrawals root matches what it has in the beacon state and filter builder bids based on that. In epbs, a proposer can't do it; it could sign a bid with an invalid withdrawals root but still get paid regardless. That's a mental shift. Sure, we can move processing withdrawals to the payload, that makes this argument moot...

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I think this is kinda irrelevant, the builder can always invalidate it's own payload. It could prevent a very specific bug in the builder that has the right beacon block root as parent and has the wrong state transition, I do not see what's the gain here

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: I think you get slightly better liveness. The difference is that the proposer has a choice to prevent a missing execution slot. If you take the withdrawal issue above and apply it to epbs today, the execution slot is missed, but in MEV-Boost, it defaults to local building

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Notice that today the problem when the builder has the wrong withdrawals is because it's building over the wrong block. On ePBS you already commit to a parent block root

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: I buy this argument. Instead of checking withdrawals root, checking the parent block hash/root is good enough to prevent this

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Oh I think I have a pretty bad bug on forkchoice 😦

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: What is it? 🙂

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: weight counting is wrong

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: just happy case?  or reveal status + new boost values are in play?

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: how could it have the wrong block? `getHeader` specifies the parent hash

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: that's simply a bug

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: that's the same guarantee you describe above

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yeah but that bug is that they are building over the wrong beaconstate, but yeah hash is just as good as  root here

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: right, but if they manage to get the wrong beaconstate (therefore withdrawals) already, it won't be better or worse this way

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I think it's still kinda irrelevant, if a builder is giving bad blocks on ePBS, proposers can immediately block it

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: because that wrong beacon is already a bug, not a hole in the API

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yeah definitely I think builders bugs are kinda irrelevant

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: how can the proposer know that from just the bid itself? because today you can withdrawals_root is part of the header

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: yeah that is a regression

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: or potentially

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: in any case it's a bug that would cause bad incentives if fixed like that: rational proposers would still prefer to include the bad bid

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: of course we can make it part of state transition

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
> rational proposers would still prefer to include the bad bid
That wont be the client code though. We check withdralwas root and use local block if it fails

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: which transition it's part of is partly a question of who should bear the risk

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: anyway, this is extra complexity without any reason, it's much simpler to just move withdrawals to the payload

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: ya, I tend to agree with this

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Anyway, I'll continue debugging forkchoice which is a bit of a mess

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: sure, it's at least not worse than today then

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: in epbs, we can do better circuit breaker too, we can block the builder if we immediate see one invalid execution payload from them

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Whomever decided to have an executable spec is a genius, it's trully the best protocol bug bounty program I've ever seen, it pays for itself
